summary: MARS360 is a single-file interactive Mars exploration website (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js). It shows a rotating 3D globe built from NASA Mars Trek imagery. You can click anywhere to inspect a location and switch between water ice, temperature, radiation and terrain views. You can also save up to three places to a Mission Passport, which compares them and writes a short rule-based Field Report. Potential exploration zones are marked as research candidates, separate from verified landing sites. Anything without verified data is labelled as such, and unfinished layers such as the SWIM ice maps are marked "awaiting data integration." Source cards link to the official NASA archives. The goal is to make existing NASA data easy to explore and to show where future human missions might look.
